slides.title: The colony and its castes
body: Lecture 1 of the Hollowmere Beekeepers' Guild foundation course
The three castes: queen, workers and drones
How a colony divides its work

slides.title: The queen
body: The queen is the colony's only female
She lays up to 1,500 eggs a day at the height of summer
She is fed on royal jelly throughout her life

slides.title: The workers
body: Workers forage, build comb, nurse brood and guard the entrance
A worker's duties change with its age

slides.title: The drones
body: Drones are larger than workers and have no sting
Drones keep the brood warm in spring
They are driven out of the hive at the first frost

slides.title: Wax glands
body: Workers make wax from four pairs of glands under the abdomen
The glands work best between the twelfth and eighteenth day of a worker's life
Wax flakes are chewed soft before they are built into comb

slides.title: Summary
body: The queen lays; the workers do every other task; the drones warm the spring brood
